audit.why: 45.26% Emerald+ over 137 games with HARD and 8/10 matches what the kits show: Bladesurge is a 10s-at-rank-1 dash that refreshes on any Marked target or kill, so Irelia re-engages faster than Sejuani can disengage on an 18s Arctic Assault. Difficulty rating left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[6] and phases[6].side both said Irelia for Two+ items, but whys[6] reads 'returning the matchup to Skill in the fights that count' and phases[6].why reads 'You're a teamfight engine now — the lane barely matters'. The captions describe an even stage and the side said otherwise.
audit.why: A two-item Sejuani is a teamfight anchor Irelia cannot solo-kill; the page's own prose says so twice. Level 6 was already Skill and stays there, and the five stages before it stay Irelia.
audit.corrected: Two+ items moved to Skill on win[6] and phases[6].side.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five fields claimed Defiant Dance (W) absorbs Sejuani's burst and heals Irelia back, and mid called it 'W invulnerability'. Riot's Defiant Dance text is 'Irelia charges a strike that deals more damage as she charges. She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' The heal lives on Bladesurge (Q): 'Irelia dashes forward to strike her target, healing herself.'
audit.why: This inverts how the trade actually resolves. Winter's Wrath, Permafrost and the Fury of the North shatter are magic damage, so Defiant Dance does not blunt Sejuani's combo at all — it blunts her autos. Telling a Sejuani player her burst gets absorbed makes her skip the one trade she wins.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance is now stated as physical-only damage reduction in spikes[0], early, mid, whys[2] and wants.foe[2], and the heal is attributed to Bladesurge. Grievous Wounds timing added to wants.you[2] against that heal.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns and loading told the player to 'count it out loud' with no number anywhere.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 falling to 10s, and Bladesurge is 10s at rank 1 but refreshes free on a Marked target or a kill — those are two different clocks and only one is countable. A player told to count needs to know which.
audit.corrected: Real numbers added to breakdown.cooldowns and loading, with the note that Bladesurge's timer is not a timer whenever a Mark is on you.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Irelia 'his' and 'him' throughout.
audit.corrected: Fixed inside the strings rewritten here; several untouched fields still say 'him'.

edits.after: Irelia's Ionian Fervor caps fast off the wave, and Bladesurge — not Defiant Dance — is the heal, refreshing free on any Marked target or a kill.

edits.before: Irelia wins level 1 by doing nothing special — she auto-attacks minions, stacks Ionian Fervor, and reaches you before your Frost armor is up. Do not contest autos, take W first, and eat nothing free. At level 2 her Q starts resetting on low-HP minions and she can string dashes into you unpredictably — use Q Arctic Assault purely as an exit, never a trade starter. At level 3 you have your full Q-W-E chain but she has Defiant Dance W to absorb the burst and Flawless Duet E ready to stun you inside the trade — only exchange if she mispositons inside a caster-minion pile where you can proc Permafrost without chasing, and immediately walk after the stun fires.
edits.after: Irelia wins level 1 by doing nothing special — she auto-attacks minions, stacks Ionian Fervor, and reaches you before your Frost Armor is up. Do not contest autos, take W first, and eat nothing free. At level 2 Bladesurge starts refreshing on low-HP minions and she can string dashes into you unpredictably — use Arctic Assault purely as an exit, never a trade starter. At level 3 you have the full W-W into Permafrost chain and she has Flawless Duet ready to stun you inside it. Defiant Dance does not save her: it cuts physical damage only, and Winter's Wrath, Permafrost and the passive shatter are all magic. Trade when she charges it, land the stun, and walk.

edits.before: Farm to first item (Sunfire Aegis) and arrive at river skirmishes where your R and E chain beats her 2v2
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds before your second item — Bladesurge heals her through every extended trade you start

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are a dead zone: her Q reset-dash pattern means she can re-engage every time you try to disengage, her W heals the damage you deal, and your Frost armor is constantly stripped because she never gives you the three-second window it requires to stack up. Dodge the Flawless Duet E placement — that is the only non-negotiable mechanical task in this matchup, because landing it lets her stun you in place and freecast until you die. At level 6 Glacial Prison changes the calculus: it is the first CC she cannot answer with W invulnerability, and she must respect the comet or risk a point-and-click stun into a gank. Play level 6 as a threat rather than a trigger — let her see the R and back off, then shove, rotate, and be first to the river fight.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are a dead zone: Bladesurge refreshes free on any Marked target, so she re-engages every time you try to leave, and your Frost Armor is constantly stripped because she never gives you the out-of-combat window it needs to rebuild. Dodging Flawless Duet is the only non-negotiable task here — 16 seconds at rank 1, 850 range, and landing it lets her stun you in place and freecast. Do not fear Defiant Dance: it reduces physical damage, so your magic combo lands through it. At level 6 Glacial Prison changes the calculus — a 1300-range point-and-click stun she cannot dash out of, and she must respect it. Play 6 as a threat rather than a trigger: let her see the R, then shove, rotate, and be first to the river.

edits.after: - Irelia Flawless Duet: matchup-defining — 16s at rank 1 down to 10s, 850 range. Dodge it and the dive falls apart. - Bladesurge is 10s but refreshes free on a Marked target, so a Mark on you means no cooldown. - Your Q is the exit, 18s.
